Internal helper: the stop for a call with no data frame and no default

Source: R/checks.R
dot-jst_no_frame_stop.Rd

jt(Score ~ Gender), jscreen() or jcorr() with no data frame named and no juse() default. Until Session 368 (Fix Slate 15) every function reaching .jst_resolve_data() this way stopped with "No data frame specified and no default set. Use juse() to set a default.": one route, two sentences on one line. It now offers both routes, as the resolver's stop for a name not found and jsave()'s since Session 367 do (.jst_jsave_no_frame_stop()): the call with the data frame named, or a default set and the call run again.

Usage

.jst_no_frame_stop(envir, vars = NULL)

Arguments

envir

The caller's environment, where the data frames are looked for.

vars

Character or NULL. The variables the data frame named must hold; NULL (the default) reads them from the call.

Value

Does not return; stops.

Details

The call is the user's (.jst_caller_call()). In a formula call the data frame goes after the formula – jt(Score ~ Gender, d), or data = d after a formula given as formula = – and the data frame named is the one data frame in the workspace that holds every variable the formula names. In any other call it goes first, in place of an empty first argument (jdesc(, Age)) when there is one, and the variables to match are those of the call's unnamed arguments; a call with none, such as jscreen(), has no variable to match, so any one data frame counts, as in jsave(). With none or several, MyData. The rest of the call is kept as typed; the second route runs the call as typed.

A caller whose unnamed arguments are not variables says so with vars: jcopy()'s one name is the copy's destination (jcopy(newdata)), so it passes character(0), and any one data frame counts (Session 369, Fix Slate 16).

A call that names neither a data frame nor a variable, to a function that needs variables – jdesc(), jfreq(), jcorr(), jalpha(), jsum(), javg(), jplot() – gets ONE stop instead (ruling R22, Session 369; Fix Slate 17): either route above, run, stopped again for want of variables. It says both are missing and gives the function's own example on community, keeping the call's display options (method =, digits = and the like), which hold on any data, and leaving out the arguments that name the user's variables (by =, subset =, numeric = ...) or depend on them (min.valid =, type =). jscreen() keeps the two routes: given a data frame alone it screens every column.

Since Session 370 (Fix Slate 18) the same stop serves jrecode(), jencode(), jrelabel() and jdeclare_missing(), each with the example its own no-variable stop gives (.jst_no_var_example()), and jconvert(), which needs a target rather than variables: "no data frame and no target format were named." with jconvert(community, to = "stata"). A call that names its variables or the target by argument (orig.var =, var =, vars =, to =) lacks only the data frame and keeps the two routes, as does jconvert() under a session convention, which supplies the target. These keep only modify = and missing.notice = from the call (jdeclare_missing() and jconvert()); their labels =, map = and codes = depend on the user's variables.
